# Bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget exhaustion

## Context / Problem

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a].

`CompletionAgentStep.run` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:426`) catches ONLY
`UnretryableOutputError`, and only when `_is_token_exhaustion(exc)` holds. A step-budget exhaustion
raises `LLMRunnerError` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:95` builds it as `budget_err` with a
`.diagnostic` attached), and per `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` `LLMRunnerError` is a strict ANCESTOR of
`UnretryableOutputError` — so it never matches and the recovery never engages.

Confirmed by experiment, with a control: a synthetic budget `LLMRunnerError` fed to
`CompletionAgentStep.run` PROPAGATED and left `failure_diagnostic is None`; the control, an
`UnretryableOutputError` truncation, ENTERED recovery.

This matters because bounded recovery is exactly the mechanism the failure needs. It isolates each
explicit criterion in a FRESH agentic history (so a loop cannot persist across criteria), converges
the evidence run at 16 run steps, and finishes with a tool-free structured finalizer — see
`docs/llm-framework.md`. The error message printed to the operator says "narrow the task", and
this is the machinery that does exactly that, sitting unreachable one `except` clause away.

## Approach

Two small pieces, per the design review on this ticket's plan:

1. **A dedicated typed exception.** `interpret_failure`'s budget branch (`structured_run.py:95`)
   currently raises a bare `LLMRunnerError`. Diagnostic-shape sniffing CANNOT identify that branch:
   `interpret_failure` attaches the SAME `usage_log.failure_usage(...)` dict (same key set) to
   EVERY exception it raises — typed `LLMError`s, sampling rejections, and `LLMUnavailableError`
   alike — so "carries requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys" is true of all of them. Add
   `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)` to `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` and raise it from the
   budget branch. Every existing `except LLMRunnerError` / `except LLMError` site keeps catching
   (strict subclass = backward compatible), and the budget stop becomes identifiable **purely by
   type** — no message sniffing, no shape sniffing.
2. **The missing entry edge.** Extend the `except` clause in `CompletionAgentStep.run` to catch
   `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` and route it to the existing `_recover(...)`. The truncation path
   keeps its exact current behaviour: `UnretryableOutputError` + `_is_token_exhaustion` still
   routes to the same `_recover`. `_recover`'s own fail-closed guarantees are untouched — this
   ticket only adds the missing entry edge. The budget diagnostic is preserved onto
   `self.failure_diagnostic` before recovery so that if recovery ALSO fails,
   `raise_completion_workflow_failure` has the loop-vs-breadth counters (the surfacing of those
   counters is [rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e]'s subject).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` — new `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)`.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — the budget branch of `interpret_failure` raises the subclass
  (message and `.diagnostic` unchanged).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the `except` spine of
  `CompletionAgentStep.run` catches the subclass and routes to `_recover`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` — the tests below (extends the existing
  suite for this class).

Out of scope: what `tool_step_limit` does inside the evidence runs ([rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2]);
the runaway detector/actuator ([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]); sidecar emission
([rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e]).

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py -q

Happy path: an `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` from the primary step enters recovery and produces a
verdict. Edge: a plain `LLMRunnerError` (not the subclass) still propagates (negative control); the
truncation path is regression-pinned. Failure path: recovery that cannot produce full criterion
coverage still fails closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError)` exists in `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` and
      `interpret_failure`'s budget branch raises it with the same message and `.diagnostic` as
      today; verified by a unit test on `interpret_failure` asserting the raised type, message, and
      diagnostic keys, and by every existing `except LLMRunnerError`-based test passing unmodified
- [x] a step-budget exhaustion (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError`) routes into the
      bounded per-criterion recovery instead of propagating; verified by a test driving it end to end
      through `CompletionAgentStep.run` with a fake runner and asserting recovery ran and produced a
      verdict
- [x] a plain `LLMRunnerError` that is NOT the budget subclass still propagates unchanged (the catch
      is purely typed — no message or diagnostic-shape sniffing); verified by a negative-control test
- [x] the truncation path keeps its current behaviour exactly (`UnretryableOutputError` +
      `_is_token_exhaustion` -> recovery; non-exhaustion `UnretryableOutputError` propagates);
      regression-pinned by the existing tests passing unmodified
- [x] recovery still fails CLOSED when it cannot produce full criterion coverage — this must never
      become a route to an unearned PASS; verified by a test where recovery's preconditions fail and
      the step still raises
- [x] when recovery also fails, the original budget diagnostic is preserved on
      `self.failure_diagnostic` (not lost); verified by a test asserting the diagnostic's
      `requests`/`tool_calls` counters survive
